label: prop:confinement-level-unique
title: Uniqueness of the confinement level
html:
Proposition. Uniqueness of the confinement level

The confinement level \ell(K, q) = \min\{\ell : T_w \in J^\ell(q)\} is unique: any two confinement levels for the same braid at the same q are equal.

The argument is antisymmetry. If \ell_1 and \ell_2 are both least elements of \{\ell : T_w \in J^\ell(q)\}, then each is valid and each bounds the other below, so \ell_1 \le \ell_2 and \ell_2 \le \ell_1.

Two further properties of the filtration are worth stating, though neither is used in the uniqueness argument:

  1. The filtration J^\bullet(q) is monotone: J^0(q) \subseteq J^1(q) \subseteq \cdots \subseteq J^m(q) = H_n(R, q), so the valid level set is upward-closed. This is what makes \ell a threshold rather than an isolated index, and it is why tied operators enter together at a single level without disturbing uniqueness.
  2. The valid set is nonempty (it contains m, since J^m = H_n). This is what prop:confinement-level-exists needs — existence follows from nonemptiness by well-ordering of \mathbb{N} — and it is not needed here.
